# A Logging Function
<!-- Slide 42 -->

## What?

- A logging feature is usually a class designed to capture troubleshooting and performance information for later analysis.
- Recorded to disk.
- Make the design standalone for portability.

::: notes
Slides 42–48
The source introduces the general idea of a logger before showing the function-based version used today.
:::

<!-- Slide 43 -->

---

## Why?

- A debugger will only capture the program state *right now*.
- A logger can capture program state history.
- We do not want to clog the terminal window with performance information, but we may need access to that information later.
- A text file can be filtered to find just what we need.

<!-- Slide 44 -->

---

## When?/Use Case

- Anytime you are developing software.
- Several languages have built-in logging features.
  - Python
  - `java.util.logging`
  - JavaScript → `console.log`

<!-- Slide 45 -->

---

## How?

- C++ uses `std::err` and `std::cout`.
- We will construct a simple logger using functions.
- Then switch to an OOP design later.

::: notes
The source says std::err. Preserve that wording for the later completeness review.
:::

<!-- Slide 46 -->

---

## Limitations

- Increases resource use.
